card.name: Angama
card.tagline: Masked ancestral spirits visit homes during Yaeyama Obon
card.profile: Angama is an Obon ancestral-spirit ritual dance of Japan's Yaeyama Islands (Ishigaki and neighbouring islands). Troupes led by two masked elders - Ushumai (an old man) and Nmi/Nmii (an old woman) representing ancestral spirits returning from the afterworld - bring flower-hatted descendants (faamaa) to invited homes, where they dance nenbutsu songs before the family altar and exchange humorous question-and-answer banter about the afterlife (Wikipedia, Angama (dance); Okinawa Clip). It is performed during the lunar-calendar Bon (sorin) in the 7th month.
card.insight: Per Wikipedia, Angama shares its mainland Japanese (nenbutsu) origin with Okinawa's Eisa; nenbutsu practice was reportedly brought to Yaeyama in 1657 when the samurai leader Miyara Chouju traveled to Okinawa to pay tribute.
